comparison: Perfect alignment on transcriptomic evidence for non-canonical JAG1 signaling (C19-C22, C45). Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval notes limitation of single donor with technical replicates and suggests need for independent validation, while peer reviewers accept findings without raising these methodological concerns.

Perfect alignment on clinical context and background claims (C1-C6). Both evaluations support these literature-based claims. OpenEval identifies potential error in C2 regarding 'allograft survival rate' terminology, while peer reviewers accept background without question.

Strong alignment on in vitro osteoblast differentiation evidence (C9-C13). Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval covers C57 (negative controls) in addition, noting it strengthens JAG1 specificity. Peer reviewers describe experimental design as appropriate and results clearly presented.

Strong alignment on in vivo bone regeneration findings (C14-C18). Both evaluations support these results. OpenEval notes lack of biomechanical testing as acknowledged limitation and covers histological data (C54-C55) not mentioned in peer evaluation. Peer reviewers describe evidence as 'convincing' and offering 'promising avenue for treatment.'

Strong alignment on methodological details (C49-C53). Both evaluations support the experimental design. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of appropriateness while noting potential selection bias in cell line choice. Peer reviewer 1 explicitly affirms 'experimental design is appropriate.'

Strong alignment on biological context claims (C35-C44). Both evaluations support these literature-based contextual claims. OpenEval notes these pathways are broadly involved in cell biology beyond osteoblasts. Peer reviewers implicitly accept context through acceptance of overall mechanistic conclusions.

Alignment on p70 S6K inhibition findings (C26-C27). Both evaluations support these observations. OpenEval provides detailed interpretation of partial inhibition and dissociation between mineralization and gene expression. Peer reviewers accept findings without raising concerns.

Both address C56 (negative RUNX2/SP7 findings). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to data not shown and contradiction with RNA-seq results, requiring careful interpretation. Peer reviewers support these negative controls without raising concerns, treating them as part of JAG1-specific characterization.

Partial overlap on phosphoprotein validation. OpenEval R4 addresses C23 (Luminex phosphoprotein data), while peer R4 addresses C23-C25 plus C46 (main conclusion). Both support findings. OpenEval notes missing p-values for some events. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm p70 S6K mechanism as 'crucial.'

Partial overlap on p70 S6K mechanism. OpenEval R5 addresses C24-C27 (functional inhibition studies), while peer R4 addresses C23-C25 plus C46. Both support findings. OpenEval interprets partial inhibition as indicating multiple pathways. Peer reviewers affirm mechanism has 'significant implications.'

Partial overlap on prior research context. OpenEval R9 addresses C7-C8 plus C28-C34 (broader literature context), while peer R8 addresses C7-C8 plus C28 (authors' prior JAG1 work). Both support these contextual claims. Peer reviewer 1 explicitly acknowledges building on prior research.

Partial overlap on literature context. OpenEval R9 addresses C7-C8 and C28-C34, while peer R10 addresses C29-C44 (broader biological context). Both support these literature-based claims. OpenEval notes evaluation of prior claims is beyond manuscript scope.

Partial overlap on in vivo study details. OpenEval R2 addresses in vivo regeneration (C14-C18) plus histology (C54-C55), while peer R6 addresses only histology and controls (C54-C55). Both support findings. Peer reviewers treat histology as supporting data without specific critique.

Partial overlap on developmental context. OpenEval R12 addresses C47-C48 (craniofacial development background), while peer R11 addresses C47-C53 (development plus methodology). Both support claims. OpenEval notes this establishes rationale for craniofacial-specific approaches.

Minimal overlap on main conclusion. OpenEval R11 addresses C46 (main conclusion in abstract), while peer R4 addresses C23-C25 plus C46 (mechanism and conclusion). Both support conclusion. OpenEval notes convergent evidence from multiple approaches; peer reviewers affirm 'crucial mechanism' and 'significant implications.'

Minimal overlap on control experiments. OpenEval R1 addresses in vitro differentiation (C9-C13) plus C57 (negative controls), while peer R7 addresses C56-C57 (negative findings). Both support findings. OpenEval emphasizes C57 strengthens JAG1 specificity.
